en: The Hymn of Veneration to the Caityas:
Birth, enlightenment, the peerless and powerful Wheel of Dharma in the forest,
and the noble miracle at the Caitya— these glorious deeds, revered by the three worlds.
At the shrine at Sthāna, which resembles a mountain city, I worship with devotion and a bowed head the descent of the God of Gods, by whom the Buddhas have attained liberation. || 1 ||
In Vaiśālī at the Dharmacakra, on the mountain of Gṛdhrakūṭa where the Victorious One is renowned,
in Śrāvastī, in Lumbinī, in the excellent city of Kuśinagara, and in the place called Kāpila; in Kauśalī at Sthūlakūṭa, in the excellent city of Mathurā, and at the cowherd Nanda’s dwelling.
And those other reliquaries and shrines of the ten powers, I pay homage to those Buddhas. (2)
On Kailāśa, Hemakūṭa, Himavat, Nila, Mandara, and the peak of Meru;

in Pātāla, Vaijayanta, and the abode of the Lord of Wealth (Dhanapati); in the world of the Siddhas and Gandharvas, within the cosmic egg (Brahmāṇḍa), on the earth of Viṣṇu, in the city of Paśupati, and surpassing even the moon and the sun.
And those other reliquaries and shrines of the elements, empowered by the Ten Powers—I pay homage to those Buddhas. (3)
In Kashmir, in the land of China, in Khasatavarapura, in Balkala, or in Siṃhala; in Rāta and other places, in Siṃhapoṭa, constantly and without interruption in Vallakha, in the place called Kāpila;
in Nepal, in Kāmarūpa, in Kuvasavarapura, and in Kāntiśobhāsarāta—
And those other reliquaries and shrines empowered by the Ten Powers—to those Buddhas I pay homage. (4)
And those which are within the womb of the elements, born from the body of the One Possessing the Ten Powers, and those shrines known as "the Jar";
the embers in the place of alkaline salt, the form of snow and silver, and the appearance of jewels upon barren soil;
and those in the netherworld, on the earth, situated on mountain peaks, or found everywhere—[all these are to be extracted].
And those images of the Buddhas which have been fashioned day by day through virtuous deeds—to those Buddhas I pay homage. (5)
